system_note: What was billed: Principal diagnosis I21.19 (STEMI involving other coronary artery of inferior wall, POA=Y). Key high-severity secondary diagnoses billed include R57.0 (cardiogenic shock, MCC), J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, MCC), and I46.9 (cardiac arrest, MCC). What the chart documents: multiple contemporaneous provider notes and procedure documentation consistently describe an acute ANTERIOR ST-elevation myocardial infarction with a proximal LAD occlusion treated with primary PCI and placement of a drug-eluting stent, plus cardiogenic shock requiring Impella CP and IABP, invasive mechanical ventilation, and an in-hospital pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest with ROSC. Citations: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 158 (pre-hospital ECG with ST-elevations in V1-V4) and same H&P echo statement documenting "Severe LV dysfunction post-anterior STEMI." Interventional PCI procedure note (with Primary PCI), Chart Notes, p. 836 documents stenting of the proximal LAD. These passages support an anterior/LAD STEMI, not an inferior-wall STEMI as billed. Evidence: - "pre-hospital 12-lead ECG demonstrated ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4 with reciprocal changes, and STEMI activation was called." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 158) - "Transthoracic Echocardiogram (Bedside, Emergent): Severe LV dysfunction post-anterior STEMI. No mechanical complications identified." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 158) - "placement of 3.0 x 28 mm drug-eluting stent to proximal LAD. TIMI 2 flow achieved" (with Primary PCI, Chart Notes, p. 836) Impact on coding: The principal diagnosis (position 1) is sequenced as STEMI in the bill, which is appropriate given the admission; however the billed STEMI code specifies the inferior wall (I21.19) while the clinical documentation repeatedly identifies an anterior (LAD) STEMI. This is a principal-diagnosis coding error (incorrect anatomical specificity) and requires correction to the appropriate anterior-LAD STEMI code (ICD-10 I21.0x) to match the documentation. Additional coding error: the record documents a post-operative superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) that developed after surgery and was treated during the admission; that condition is described in the discharge summary as a post-operative complication and therefore the procedure-related infection code should be POA = N, not POA = Y as billed. Evidence: - "The post-operative course was complicated by ... a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC therapy" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1008-1009) Validation of high-severity secondary codes: cardiogenic shock (R57.0), acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01), and cardiac arrest with ROSC (I46.9) are each supported by objective data and management documented in the chart: vasopressor/inotrope and mechanical circulatory support placement (Interventional Cardiology Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 45), invasive mechanical ventilation and ABG/P/F values demonstrating hypoxemia (Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, p. 550), and an 8-minute ACLS event with ROSC and TTM (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1008-1009). Policy support (select examples): R57.0 presumption when MCS is initiated; J96.01 presumption when invasive ventilation is attributed to respiratory failure; I46.9 requires documented pulseless arrest with ROSC and post-arrest management - all of which are met in the chart. Action required / correction: 1) Recode the principal diagnosis to the ICD-10 code specifying an ANTERIOR (LAD) STEMI (I21.0x) to reflect the documentation (provider confirmation/query may be used to select the exact 4th-character specificity). 2) Correct the POA indicator for the post-operative infection (T81.4XXA and related infection cause code B95.61) to Not Present on Admission (N). 3) Retain the supported high-severity secondary diagnoses and procedure codes (R57.0, J96.01, I46.9, N17.9, I50.23, I48.91, DVT, CABG and MCS/ventilation codes) as they are documented and meet the policy validation criteria cited below. Recommended coder step: submit a CDI/provider query to confirm the exact ICD-10 code for the anterior STEMI (specify LAD/anterior site) so the correct 4th/5th character can be assigned. Documentation-based confidence: high (clear, repeated statements and objective data). Auditor citations and underpinning excerpts are provided in evidence_cited for line-by-line traceability.
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical documentation and coding review for inpatient claim MR_02 Dear Provider / Health Information Management Team, We performed a clinical documentation and claims audit of the above inpatient encounter (admit 2026-01-17 to 2026-04-25). Our review focused on principal diagnosis sequencing, presence-on-admission (POA) indicators, and validation of CC/MCC-level diagnoses against governing policy criteria and the medical record. Finding: Principal diagnosis code specificity inconsistent with the medical record; incorrect POA indication for post-operative infection. Basis for finding (selected chart evidence): - The admission and procedure documentation consistently describe an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with proximal LAD occlusion treated by primary PCI: "pre-hospital 12-lead ECG demonstrated ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4 with reciprocal changes, and STEMI activation was called." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 158) and "placement of 3.0 x 28 mm drug-eluting stent to proximal LAD. TIMI 2 flow achieved" (with Primary PCI, Chart Notes, p. 836). Echocardiogram documents "Severe LV dysfunction post-anterior STEMI." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 158). The claim was billed with I21.19 (STEMI involving other coronary artery of inferior wall), which is anatomically discordant with the documentation of an anterior/LAD STEMI. - The discharge summary documents a post-operative superficial sternal wound infection due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus treated during the admission: "The post-operative course was complicated by ... a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC therapy." (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1008-1009). This description indicates the infection was a postoperative complication (not present on admission), therefore the procedure-related infection code(s) should be reported POA = N. The claim shows a POA=Y for the infection following a procedure code. Policy references relied upon (selected): - R57.0 (Cardiogenic shock) policy: presumption rule that initiation of mechanical circulatory support (Impella, IABP) attributed to hemodynamic instability satisfies the hemodynamic criterion needed to validate cardiogenic shock. (Policy Documents/DRG/Cardiogenic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria) - J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) policy: presumption rule that when invasive mechanical ventilation is documented and attributed to acute respiratory failure, objective hypoxemia criterion is satisfied. (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx, Validation Criteria) - I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) policy: documentation of pulseless arrest with documented ROSC and post-arrest management supports coding of cardiac arrest and related post-arrest diagnoses. (Policy Documents/DRG/Cardiac Arrest with Return of Spontaneous Circulation.docx, Medical - Primary Cardiac Arrest with ROSC Pathway) Correction being made: 1) Principal diagnosis will be changed to the ICD-10 code that specifies an acute ANTERIOR STEMI (ICD-10 I21.0x family) to reflect the documented LAD/anterior territory infarction. Please provide provider attestation of the exact anterior STEMI code (anterior/LAD site) if available; we will update to the precise 4th/5th-character code per your confirmation. 2) The POA indicator for the procedure-related infection code(s) (T81.4XXA and related B95.61) will be corrected to Not Present on Admission (N) because the infection is documented as developing post-operatively and treated during the admission. 3) The following high-severity secondary diagnoses and procedure codes are supported by the chart and will be retained: R57.0 (cardiogenic shock - supported by mechanical circulatory support placement and vasopressor/inotrope use), J96.01 (acute hypoxemic respiratory failure - supported by invasive ventilation and ABG/P/F values), I46.9 (cardiac arrest with ROSC - supported by code event and post-arrest management), N17.9 (contrast-induced AKI documented by nephrology and creatinine rise), I50.23 (acute on chronic systolic heart failure), I48.91 (post-operative atrial fibrillation), I82.401 (catheter-associated DVT), and the ICD-10-PCS procedure codes for Impella/IABP, CABG, endotracheal tube, and prolonged ventilation. If you disagree with the above corrections, please respond with the provider's clinical attestation specifying the exact anterior STEMI ICD-10 code (including any laterality/site characters) or documentation that would justify retaining the billed inferior-wall STEMI code. For the infection POA indicator, please provide documentation showing the infection was present on admission if you contend POA=Y. Sincerely, Clinical Documentation Audit Team
